title: Fibrewise equivalence criterion for categories fibred in groupoids
statement: Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a category small in the larger universe and let $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ and $q:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be categories fibred in groupoids, with small fibre groupoids in that universe: every base arrow $u:S\to T$ admits a cartesian lift with any prescribed target over $T$, and each fibre (objects over $T$ and arrows over $1_T$) is a groupoid. Here an arrow $v:a'\to a$ over $u:S\to T$ is cartesian if for every $h:R\to S$, every arrow $w:z\to a$ over $u h$ factors uniquely as $v\widetilde w$ with $\widetilde w:z\to a'$ over $h$. Let $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ satisfy $qG=p$ and preserve cartesian arrows. If, for every $T$, the induced functor $G_T:\mathcal A(T)\to\mathcal B(T)$ is fully faithful (bijections on all morphism sets) and essentially surjective (every object of $\mathcal B(T)$ is isomorphic over $1_T$ to an image), then there is a cartesian functor $H:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ over $\mathcal C$ and natural isomorphisms $HG\cong1_{\mathcal A}$ and $GH\cong1_{\mathcal B}$ whose components lie over identities in $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: For $a\in\mathcal A(S)$, $a'\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $u:S\to T$, choose a cartesian lift $v:u^*a'\to a'$ over $u$. Its defining property identifies arrows $a\to a'$ over $u$ with vertical arrows $a\to u^*a'$, by $t\mapsto v\circ t$. Since $G(v)$ is cartesian, the same holds in $\mathcal B$ with $G(a)$ and $G(u^*a')$. These identifications intertwine $G$ with the morphism map of $G_S$, which is bijective by hypothesis. Thus $G$ is bijective on arrows over each $u$. Every arrow has one base arrow and $qG=p$, so $G$ is fully faithful on the total categories.

For every $b\in\mathcal B(T)$ choose $a_b\in\mathcal A(T)$ and a vertical isomorphism $i_b:b\xrightarrow{\sim}G(a_b)$ by essential surjectivity of $G_T$. These are simultaneous choices in the larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention]: the base is small, and its small fibres give a small union of objects. Retain these fibrewise choices; their base objects are exactly $T$.

Apply [lem-sfb-chosen-object-quasi-inverse] to the fully faithful total functor $G$ and the specified $a_b,i_b$. It gives a functor $H$ with $H(b)=a_b$, natural isomorphisms $i:1_{\mathcal B}\xrightarrow{\sim}GH$ and $e:HG\xrightarrow{\sim}1_{\mathcal A}$, and equations $G(H(f))=i_{b'}\circ f\circ i_b^{-1}$ and $G(e_a)=i_{G(a)}^{-1}$. This is a use of the prescribed-choice statement, not just existence of an arbitrary ordinary quasi-inverse.

source.place: Tag 003Z, lemma-equivalence-fibred-categories, quasi-inverse paragraph; Tag 05SG, lemma-construct-quasi-inverse.

proof.text: On objects $pH(b)=q(b)$ by the choices. Applying $q$ to $G(H(f))=i_{b'}\circ f\circ i_b^{-1}$ gives $p(H(f))=q(f)$ because both comparison components are vertical. Hence $pH=q$ as functors. Also $p(e_a)=q(G(e_a))=q(i_{G(a)}^{-1})=1_{p(a)}$. Thus $e:HG\cong1_{\mathcal A}$ and $i^{-1}:GH\cong1_{\mathcal B}$ have precisely the required vertical components.

Finally every arrow $w:a\to a'$ of $\mathcal A$ is cartesian. Choose a cartesian lift $v:c\to a'$ of $p(w)$; the defining factorization is $w=v\circ t$ with $t:a\to c$ vertical. Since the fibre is a groupoid, $t$ is invertible. For any $z\to a'$ and compatible base arrow $h$, first take its unique factorization through $v$ over $h$, then compose with $t^{-1}$ to get the unique factorization through $w$ over $h$. This is exactly cartesianness as defined in the statement. In particular $H$ sends cartesian arrows of $\mathcal B$ to cartesian arrows of $\mathcal A$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q147-2c943fb7f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's five steps and the new node lem-sfb-chosen-object-quasi-inverse in full against Stacks categories.tex 003Z (all of the proof), 05SG and 003V. The tag/label pairs are confirmed in tags/tags. Step 1: cartesian with h=1 makes arrows over u the same as vertical arrows into u^*a'. G(v) is cartesian, so G_S being bijective gives total full faithfulness. Step 2: vertical choices over each T, and the total categories are V-small. Step 3: applies the new node with exactly its hypotheses. Step 4: p(Hf)=q(f) and p(e_a)=1 follow from the vertical i, which writes out the over-base checks that 003Z omits. Step 5: w=vt with t invertible, so every arrow is cartesian (with uniqueness), as in 003V, and H is cartesian. Every hypothesis of the item is used and the conclusion is not weakened. The new node is true. Uniqueness of J comes from naturality plus faithfulness, and e is natural with F(e_A)=i_{F(A)}^{-1}, checked after applying F. On a one-object group with F=id and i=g, J(f)=gfg^{-1} and e=g^{-1}, so the orientation is right. Empty categories are trivial. The new node is statement-only, self-contained, cites def-nagata-category, and has the correct source 05SG. It is not a duplicate of lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence (02C3), which gives only an existential inverse and so no inverse over C. DAG-wide searches (05SG, 003Z, construct-quasi-inverse, ff with quasi-inverse, fibred groupoid with equivalence) and a Mathlib grep found no duplicate or exact match. It does not restate a clause of the item. There is no cycle and no SGA. Parent step 5 is unaffected. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_cartesian_quasiInverse_of_fibrewise_equivalence {C A B : Type u} [Category.{u} C] [Category.{u} A] [Category.{u} B] (p : A ⥤ C) (q : B ⥤ C) [p.IsFibered] [q.IsFibered] (hp : ∀ T : C, IsGroupoid (Fiber p T)) (hq : ∀ T : C, IsGroupoid (Fiber q T)) (G : A ⥤ B) (hG : G ⋙ q = p) (hcart : ∀ {S T : C} (u : S ⟶ T) {a a' : A} (v : a ⟶ a'), p.IsStronglyCartesian u v → q.IsStronglyCartesian u (G.map v)) (hfull : ∀ T : C, (mapFiber G hG T).Full) (hfaithful : ∀ T : C, (mapFiber G hG T).Faithful) (hessSurj : ∀ T : C, (mapFiber G hG T).EssSurj) : ∃ H : B ⥤ A, H ⋙ p = q ∧ (∀ {S T : C} (u : S ⟶ T) {b b' : B} (v : b ⟶ b'), q.IsStronglyCartesian u v → p.IsStronglyCartesian u (H.map v)) ∧ ∃ (e : G ⋙ H ≅ 𝟭 A) (i : H ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 B), (∀ a : A, p.IsHomLift (𝟙 (p.obj a)) (e.hom.app a)) ∧ (∀ b : B, q.IsHomLift (𝟙 (q.obj b)) (i.hom.app b))
lean.note: mapFiber is the canonical induced fibre functor already introduced by this node; it specializes Mathlib Fiber.inducedFunctor and contains no choices. The size dependency is a metatheoretic convention, realized by the explicit common universe u.
